re_line: Rare earths nationalisation threatened · Navy shower-camera probe · $3b aged care plan sunk · Peters bypassed Luxon on UN vote · NZ election nears amid aid fight
morning_memo: Resources Minister Madeleine King has left open nationalising a Perth rare-earths company after China-linked investors defied Canberra's divestment orders, testing the foreign-investment screening regime.
New Zealand's Winston Peters confirmed he did not notify Christopher Luxon before New Zealand became one of only two countries to abstain on a UN pandemic-preparedness declaration.

A three-day, multinational rescue off Solomon Islands brought all 73 passengers of the ferry MV Awka ashore safely, with French and Australian aircraft airdropping supplies and a Vanuatu medical vessel joining the operation.

top_stories.headline: Resources minister leaves door open to nationalising rare earths firm
top_stories.body: Resources Minister **Madeleine King** has left open the possibility of nationalising a Perth-based critical minerals company after several China-linked investors defied federal government orders to divest their stakes. The standoff tests Canberra's foreign-investment screening regime in a sector central to diversifying critical minerals supply away from China.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News (Stephen Dziedzic): "Rare earths company could be nationalised as China-linked investors fail to divest"

top_stories.headline: Hidden recording device found in navy ship's female quarters
top_stories.body: Military police are investigating after a recording device was found on October 11 in a female-only cabin aboard HMAS Leeuwin, docked in Cairns. Senator **Jacqui Lambie** told the Senate she had received a letter alleging the device was in "shower facilities" and that footage "may have been uploaded online" before discovery; she is drafting a private member's bill on Defence Force standards.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Recording device found in women's 'shower facilities' of Australian navy ship" · also SMH (Matthew Knott): "Hidden camera found in female showers on navy ship"

top_stories.headline: Senate ambush sinks Labor's $3 billion aged care plan
top_stories.body: The Coalition, the Greens, One Nation, and the crossbench combined in the Senate to kill Labor's over-65 health rebate plan, sinking a *$3 billion* aged care package. Health Minister **Butler** has vowed to reintroduce the bill, while the ABC reports the related private health insurance changes were effectively thrown out of parliament by the same combination.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH: "Butler vows to bring back health rebate bill after Senate ambush sinks $3b aged care plan" · also ABC News: "Government fails to secure support for beleaguered private health bill"

top_stories.headline: Peters bypassed Luxon before NZ's UN pandemic abstention
top_stories.body: Foreign Minister **Winston Peters** said signing the non-binding UN declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response would have been "problematic," rejecting suggestions the abstention was performative. New Zealand was one of only two countries to abstain at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. Peters confirmed he did not notify **Christopher Luxon** or the health minister this week, though he says he told Associate Health Minister **Simeon Brown** "weeks ago."
top_stories.src_line: per RNZ: "Morning Report: Winston Peters and John Campbell in fiery clash over UN document"

overnight_items.headline: Canberra belatedly joins criticism of US sanctions on ICC
overnight_items.body_text: Australia has added its voice to international criticism of U.S. sanctions aimed at the International Criminal Court, ABC News reports, after an extended silence. The belated alignment puts Canberra alongside other partners pushing back on Washington's campaign against the court.

overnight_items.headline: Wong calls Palestinian election delay 'deeply disappointing'
overnight_items.body_text: Foreign Minister **Penny Wong** called **Mahmoud Abbas**'s decision to postpone Palestinian legislative and presidential polls until 2027 "deeply disappointing." Abbas blames Israeli attacks, settler violence, and humanitarian conditions; Israel calls that explanation a "ridiculous lie." France has called for elections to be held immediately.

overnight_items.headline: Boyer Lecture warns Australia's strategic boldness lacks a political home
overnight_items.body_text: In this year's Boyer Lecture keynote, **Sam Roggeveen** argues the post-Cold War assumption that China would accept uncontested U.S. leadership in Asia "is clearly not how things are turning out." The lecture frames Australia's strategic debate as unsettled rather than resolved.

aukus_watch.headline: Hong Kong-linked firm seeks to buy Australian military shipyard
aukus_watch.body_text: Australian Defence Magazine reports that a firm linked to Hong Kong is seeking to purchase an Australian military shipyard. The report, carried only as a headline, gives no further detail on the yard involved or the proposed terms of sale.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji minister defends MPs' pay as salary debate reignites
pacific_wire.body_text: Fisheries and Forestry Minister **Alitia Bainivalu** posted an "honest" Facebook defense of ministerial salaries, citing traditional and community obligations, and divided opinion online. An ordinary Fijian MP earns *over 600 percent* more than a full-time minimum-wage worker; backbenchers received a 138 percent pay rise in May 2024 before a mandatory 20 percent cut in April 2026 amid the fuel crisis.

pacific_wire.headline: Solomon Islands ferry passengers rescued after three days adrift
pacific_wire.body_text: The ferry MV Awka, carrying *73 passengers* and crew, arrived under tow three days after losing power off remote Temotu Province. French and Australian aircraft airdropped supplies and the government patrol boat Gizo joined the rescue, alongside the Vanuatu-based medical vessel HELPR-1.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG police seize weapons cache linked to international syndicate
pacific_wire.body_text: Papua New Guinea's police chief said the seizure of a high-powered weapons cache highlights the threat posed by transnational criminal syndicates exploiting the country for illicit firearms movement, RNZ Pacific reports.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG MP presses defence minister over recruitment saga
pacific_wire.body_text: Finschhafen MP **Rainbo Paita** challenged Defence Minister **Elias Kapavore** over the decision to resume PNG Defence Force recruitment before parliament received findings from an independent investigation into the earlier, controversial recruitment process.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu's climate minister rejects 'failure' verdict on Pre-COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu's Climate Change Minister **Maina Vakafua Talia** pushed back on criticism that last week's Pre-COP31 meeting was a failure, ABC Pacific reports, as the Pacific looks ahead to COP31 negotiations.

pacific_wire.headline: Forecasters warn of elevated cyclone risk across northern Pacific
pacific_wire.body_text: Earth Sciences New Zealand, with MetService and the University of Newcastle, forecasts *seven to eleven* named cyclones in the Southwest Pacific this season, with elevated risk for Samoa, Tokelau, and parts of Kiribati. New Caledonia and Vanuatu face a normal-to-reduced risk, while Fiji and Tonga are forecast near-normal activity.

new_zealand.headline: New Zealand's Peters disputes National's foreign aid math
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand's Foreign Minister **Winston Peters** has disputed a National Party claim that foreign aid rose *26 percent* since 2021, with his office calling the figure incorrect and citing an inflation-adjusted 10 percent rise instead. National wants to redirect the savings into $604 million for new medicines while "fully protecting aid to the Pacific"; ACT proposes deeper cuts to 2017 levels, saving about $238 million a year.

new_zealand.headline: Te Tai Tonga race wide open after Ferris's expulsion from Te Pāti Māori
new_zealand.body_text: New Zealand's largest electorate, covering the entire South Island, is contested anew after incumbent **Tākuta Ferris**'s expulsion from Te Pāti Māori. Ferris won the seat in 2023 by *2,824 votes* over Labor's **Rino Tirikatene**; none of the candidates can fall back on the party list, making the electorate their only path to parliament.

new_zealand.headline: NZDF tenders for $20 million polar surveillance drone
new_zealand.body_text: The New Zealand Defence Force is seeking a *$20 million* polar surveillance drone able to fly up to 100 nautical miles from the naval ship Aotearoa in the Southern Ocean. The tender, closing next month, foreshadows further drone purchases under the 2025-29 Defence Capability Plan, whose technology accelerator funding so far falls short of the plan's $100-300 million target.

new_zealand.headline: Housing groups urge Kāinga Ora to halt pre-election state house sale
new_zealand.body_text: Ten Wellington housing and social service groups have written to New Zealand's state housing agency Kāinga Ora, urging chief executive **Tracey Taylor** to halt the deadline sale of *36* empty Strathmore homes, set for October 21, two weeks before the November 7 election.

canberra_politics.headline: Albanese and Taylor meet more often as One Nation gains ground
canberra_politics.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** and **Angus Taylor** met at Parliament House on Monday as the crossbench raised concerns about a possible Labor-Coalition deal on artificial intelligence, SMH's Paul Sakkal reports. The more frequent contact comes as One Nation support presses on Labor's primary vote.

canberra_politics.headline: Shoebridge tells Ukrainian community not to 'burn your bridges' with Greens
canberra_politics.body_text: New Greens leader **Shoebridge** urged the Ukrainian-Australian community not to alienate his party during a tense meeting over the Greens' opposition to military aid for Ukraine, SMH's Matthew Knott reports. The Greens set defence "red lines" this month, including refusing arms transfers to Ukraine and curtailing the U.S. alliance.

canberra_politics.headline: Chalmers faces two-year fight over $40 billion trust tax overhaul
canberra_politics.body_text: Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** faces a nearly two-year campaign against his proposed trust tax reforms, which businesses warn will cause accounting turmoil, even as he insists the changes make taxation fairer. The overhaul is projected to raise *$40 billion*.

canberra_politics.headline: DemosAU poll: Labor wins House majority on just 27% primary vote
canberra_politics.body_text: A new DemosAU MRP poll projects Labor retaining a clear majority of House seats on a primary vote of only *27 percent*, with support for One Nation appearing to have eased. The seat-vote gap underscores how Australia's electoral geography can insulate a governing majority from primary vote erosion.

canberra_politics.headline: FOI shows Albanese made no submission to Bondi antisemitism inquiry
canberra_politics.body_text: Freedom-of-information documents show **Anthony Albanese** made no submission and no preparations for the Bondi antisemitism inquiry, The Australian reports. The disclosure adds to political pressure on the government over its handling of the inquiry's establishment.

business_economy.headline: Australia tables bill reserving up to 20% of LNG exports for local market
business_economy.body_text: The government has tabled legislation forcing LNG exporters to reserve up to *20 percent* of production for the domestic market, Bloomberg reports. The bill follows warnings from gas producers of market paralysis as the reservation scheme takes effect.

business_economy.headline: BHP cuts 300 jobs at Australian iron ore mines as costs rise
business_economy.body_text: BHP has cut *300* workers from its Australian iron ore operations as costs rise, Bloomberg reports, the latest sign of pressure on the sector's margins.

business_economy.headline: Failure of Australia's largest IPO in decades sends tremors through AI trade
business_economy.body_text: The collapse of Firmus's float, Australia's largest IPO in decades, is sending tremors through the broader AI investment trade, the Wall Street Journal reports, as scrutiny intensifies on the deal's backers.

business_economy.headline: New Zealand exodus to Australia hits 13-year high ahead of election
business_economy.body_text: Net migration of New Zealanders to Australia has hit its highest level in *13 years*, Bloomberg reports, as thousands leave ahead of the November 7 election. The outflow adds pressure to a campaign already centered on jobs and the cost of living.

business_economy.headline: Rio Tinto says oil price shock favours Australian miners
business_economy.body_text: Rio Tinto says rivals with longer shipping routes are curbing production as higher fuel prices play to Australia's geographic advantage, the AFR reports.

calendar_watch.event: Kāinga Ora deadline sale of 36 Wellington state homes
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Tests whether the government presses ahead with asset sales just weeks before an election that could change housing policy.

calendar_watch.event: Advance voting opens for New Zealand general election
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Marks the start of the formal pre-election voting period, after a campaign dominated by foreign aid and migration disputes.

calendar_watch.event: NZDF polar surveillance drone tender closes
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: First dedicated Southern Ocean UAV purchase under the 2025-29 Defence Capability Plan, signaling further drone acquisitions.
Determines the shape of the next coalition government, with NZ First's Winston Peters a likely kingmaker.

key_stat.label: Labor's primary vote in a DemosAU MRP poll that still shows it winning a House majority
key_stat.context: The projection illustrates how Australia's electorate geography can preserve a governing majority even as primary vote support erodes, a dynamic shadowing Albanese's standing against Taylor and One Nation.

also_today.headline: Devpolicy: Tonga anti-corruption chief on independence 'in practice'
also_today.body_text: Tonga's Anti-Corruption Commissioner **Mele Fakatouato Mangisi** writes that independence for small-island anti-corruption bodies means more than formal safeguards like the UN Convention against Corruption and the Jakarta Principles, arguing that "everyone knows everyone" in practice shapes how independence actually functions.

also_today.headline: Hospitality sector warns of worker shortages under migration cuts
also_today.body_text: Hospitality industry leaders have launched a social media campaign warning that sweeping migration cuts will leave cafes and kitchens short-staffed, ABC News reports, the latest sector pushback against the government's migration policy.

also_today.headline: University head warns foreign student cuts would cripple research
also_today.body_text: University of Tasmania Vice-Chancellor **Rufus Black** says slashing international student numbers would cripple research capacity, ABC News reports, warning of reputational damage in Asia amid the government's migration debate.
